title: Release CSV parser
prompt:
APPROVED ARCHITECT SCOPE. This brief and milestone govern the task. Earlier research artifacts are recommendations, not approvals; do not replace these requirements with them.

Project brief: Implement parseCsv(text) and toObjects(rows) in src/csv.js.
- parseCsv returns an array of rows, each an array of strings. Fields are separated by commas. A field wrapped in double quotes may contain commas and line breaks, and "" inside it means one double quote.
- Lines end with \n or \r\n. A final line break does not add an empty row, and empty text gives [].
- toObjects takes parsed rows whose first row is the header and returns one object per remaining row, keyed by the header. A short row gets empty strings for its missing columns.

Milestone: Release CSV parser
Deliver the completed CSV implementation (src/csv.js and src/csv.test.js) as the project result via workspace-files.

Acceptance: npm test passes and the delivered files match the accepted m1 evidence.

Task from the owner:
Deliver the completed CSV implementation in this workspace (src/csv.js and src/csv.test.js) as the project result. Acceptance: npm test passes and the delivered files match the accepted m1 evidence for parseCsv and toObjects.
summary: Implement the approved CSV parser and object conversion behavior with focused tests, then independently verify the specified files and full test suite before completing in-place delivery.

plan.objective: Deliver compliant parseCsv(text) and toObjects(rows) implementations in src/csv.js with matching tests in src/csv.test.js, leaving verified changes in workspace files.

steps.title: Implement CSV behavior and tests
steps.instructions: Inspect the existing project, src/csv.js, src/csv.test.js, package test setup, and any accepted m1 evidence available in the workspace. Implement parseCsv and toObjects exactly to the approved brief, adding or updating focused tests for empty input, commas, quoted commas, quoted line breaks, escaped quotes, CRLF/LF endings, no spurious final row, headers, and short rows. Run relevant tests and npm test; leave the completed src/csv.js and src/csv.test.js changes in the working tree.
steps.expectedOutcome: The implementation and tests cover the approved CSV contract and npm test passes.

steps.title: Independently verify CSV release
steps.instructions: Independently inspect src/csv.js and src/csv.test.js against the approved brief and accepted m1 evidence available in the workspace. Run npm test. If a concrete defect or missing required test is found, correct it and rerun npm test. Confirm the required files are present as working-tree deliverables. Emit the completion signal in StepOutcome: completion.status "complete" only when the objective and tests pass; otherwise emit completion.status "blocked" with the precise blocker.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSV implementation conforms to the mandated behavior, tests pass, and the workspace files are ready for in-place delivery.

plan.globalInstructions: Treat the approved project brief and milestone as authoritative. Modify only what is needed, preserve workspace and Sero state, and do not commit or create a PR.
